name: Vancouver surveys the Northwest Coast
summary: A former midshipman of Cook's spends three summers charting every inlet of the coast from California to Alaska, proving there is no passage to the Atlantic in these latitudes. His survey of Puget Sound and the island that bears his name is the basis of every later chart.

stops.note: The Discovery and the Chatham sail.
Charts part of Australia's south-west coast on the way.
The first of three winters in the islands.
Charts the sound and names it for his lieutenant, Peter Puget.
Negotiates with Bodega y Quadra over Spain's and Britain's claims.
Misses Alexander Mackenzie, arriving overland, by a few weeks.
Proves that Cook's 'river' is a closed inlet.
The last long inlet; no passage anywhere.
Home after four and a half years.
